transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

[Heading: Water supply issue]
Error 4C on Samsung washing machines specifically means 'Water Supply Issue' – the machine isn't getting enough fresh water into the drum within the expected time. 1. Is the tap behind or near the machine fully turned on?
2. Is the inlet hose kinked or crushed at the back?
3. With the machine unplugged, disconnect the hose from the back of the machine and check the small mesh filter inside the machine's water inlet for debris (sand/rust). If it looks blocked, rinse it under a tap. If the tap is on, the hose is clear, and the filter is clean but it still shows 4C, please let me know if you have low water pressure elsewhere in the house.
Tap was open, I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway, no change. Hose isn't kinked. Kitchen cold tap pressure is normal. I'll check the inlet filter at the machine end next.

[Heading: Blocked inlet mesh filter]
Since your household water pressure is normal and the tap is open, the most likely cause of error 4C is a blockage in the small mesh filter located where the inlet hose screws onto the back of the machine. This filter catches debris from your home's pipes and can get clogged over time, restricting flow enough to trigger the error. Please switch off and unplug the machine first. Disconnect the inlet hose at the machine end (have a towel ready for a little water), and look inside the small plastic socket on the machine. Check if there is a mesh screen and whether it has grit or scale blocking it. If you find debris, rinse the filter under a tap until clean before reassembling. Let me know if the filter was blocked (and cleaned) or if it looked perfectly clear.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Checked it. The mesh filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. I cleaned it and now it fills normally and the 4C has gone.

That’s excellent news. The 4C error was definitely caused by the grit and limescale blocking the inlet filter, which restricted the water flow enough to trip the fault. Since cleaning it has restored normal filling, you’ve resolved the issue yourself and don’t need to call an engineer out for this. Just keep an eye on it over the next few cycles; if the error returns, it could mean debris is building up again or there’s a secondary blockage further down the line, but for now, you’re good to go.
